name: web/scene-3d
title: 3D scene
summary: One HTML file with a low-poly three.js scene of familiar objects and actions: walk, run, fly, drive, dance, hug, follow or orbit. Uses a pinned three.js CDN.
when: Use for scenes built from the kit's shapes and actions. For a bespoke visual style, a custom model or shader, or an offline deliverable, choose a recipe or an implementation that supports those requirements.

title.about: A short name for the scene, shown in the browser tab and on the page.

scene.about: One known object or action per line. Examples: "dog walks to house and stops", "kiwi walks to tree and hugs it", "kiwi dances", "tree at 4 0". A line with "repeat" replays finite actions.
scene.default:
house at 5 -1
tree at -2 -4
dog at -7 2
dog walks to house

sky.about: The sky: day, dawn, sunset or night; or a colour in words or hex, which tints the sky, fog and light ("purple", "a purple sky", "#6b3fa0", "pink sunset").

ground.about: The ground: grass, sand, snow, water, stone, dirt or moon.

filename.about: The requested file name in the output folder, such as scene.html.

next: Use look_at_page to check rendering and motion. If the scene needs repair, update the plain lines inside <script id="scene"> in the written file. Report what the checks confirmed.
change: Make one call per change: replace_in_file(path="{file}", old="sky day", new="sky night") changes the sky (day, dawn, sunset, night); old="ground grass" changes the ground (grass, sand, snow, water, stone, dirt, moon). To add a thing or an action, put it after the ground line: old="ground grass", new="ground grass\nbird flies to tree".

not_text: The scene is empty. Add lines such as: kiwi walks to tree
is not a known thing; it is shown as a box.
